decls.name: TauCeti.Submonoid.continuousConstSMul
decls.doc: A submonoid inherits continuity in the point from an ambient continuous action.
decls.statement:
instance continuousConstSMul {M X : Type*} [MulOneClass M] [TopologicalSpace X] [SMul M X]
    [ContinuousConstSMul M X] (S : Submonoid M) : ContinuousConstSMul S X

decls.name: TauCeti.AddSubmonoid.continuousConstVAdd
decls.doc:
An additive submonoid inherits continuity in the point from an ambient continuous additive
action.

decls.name: TauCeti.Subgroup.continuousConstSMul
decls.doc: A subgroup inherits continuity in the point from an ambient continuous action.
decls.statement:
instance continuousConstSMul {G X : Type*} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace X] [SMul G X]
    [ContinuousConstSMul G X] (S : Subgroup G) : ContinuousConstSMul S X

decls.name: TauCeti.Homeomorph.applyMulAction
decls.doc: The tautological action of the homeomorphism group `E ≃ₜ E` on `E` by evaluation.
decls.statement: instance applyMulAction : MulAction (E ≃ₜ E) E

decls.name: TauCeti.Homeomorph.smul_def
decls.doc: The tautological action of `E ≃ₜ E` on `E` is given by evaluation.
decls.statement: lemma smul_def (φ : E ≃ₜ E) (e : E) : φ • e = φ e

decls.name: TauCeti.Homeomorph.applyFaithfulSMul
decls.doc: The tautological action of `E ≃ₜ E` on `E` is faithful.
decls.statement: instance applyFaithfulSMul : FaithfulSMul (E ≃ₜ E) E

decls.name: TauCeti.Homeomorph.applyContinuousConstSMul
decls.doc: The tautological action of `E ≃ₜ E` on `E` is continuous in the point.
decls.statement: instance applyContinuousConstSMul : ContinuousConstSMul (E ≃ₜ E) E

decls.name: TauCeti.Homeomorph.applySubgroupContinuousConstSMul
decls.doc:
A subgroup of the homeomorphism group acts continuously on `E` in the point, by the generic
subgroup transfer for `ContinuousConstSMul`.
decls.statement: abbrev applySubgroupContinuousConstSMul (H : Subgroup (E ≃ₜ E)) : ContinuousConstSMul H E

decls.name: TauCeti.Homeomorph.homeoCongr
decls.doc:
Conjugation by a homeomorphism `e : M ≃ₜ N` as a group isomorphism between the
self-homeomorphism groups: `homeoCongr e φ = e ∘ φ ∘ e⁻¹`. This is the homeomorphism analogue of
`Equiv.permCongrHom` and the target of the forgetful naturality of `Diffeomorph.diffCongr`.
decls.statement: def homeoCongr (e : M ≃ₜ N) : (M ≃ₜ M) ≃* (N ≃ₜ N)

decls.name: TauCeti.Homeomorph.homeoCongr_apply_apply
decls.doc: The conjugating isomorphism acts pointwise by `homeoCongr e φ x = e (φ (e.symm x))`.
decls.statement:
theorem homeoCongr_apply_apply (e : M ≃ₜ N) (φ : M ≃ₜ M) (x : N) :
    homeoCongr e φ x = e (φ (e.symm x))

decls.name: TauCeti.Homeomorph.homeoCongr_inv
decls.doc: The inverse of `homeoCongr e φ` is `homeoCongr e φ⁻¹`, since conjugation is a homomorphism.
decls.statement:
theorem homeoCongr_inv (e : M ≃ₜ N) (φ : M ≃ₜ M) :
    (homeoCongr e φ)⁻¹ = homeoCongr e φ⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.Homeomorph.homeoCongr_refl
decls.doc: Conjugating by the identity homeomorphism is the identity isomorphism.
decls.statement: theorem homeoCongr_refl : homeoCongr (_root_.Homeomorph.refl M) = MulEquiv.refl (M ≃ₜ M)

decls.name: TauCeti.Homeomorph.homeoCongr_trans
decls.doc:
Conjugation is functorial: conjugating by a composite homeomorphism is the composite of the
conjugating isomorphisms.
decls.statement:
theorem homeoCongr_trans (e : M ≃ₜ N) (e' : N ≃ₜ P) :
    homeoCongr (e.trans e') = (homeoCongr e).trans (homeoCongr e')

decls.name: TauCeti.Homeomorph.homeoCongr_symm
decls.doc: The isomorphism conjugating by `e.symm` is the inverse of the one conjugating by `e`.
decls.statement: theorem homeoCongr_symm (e : M ≃ₜ N) : (homeoCongr e).symm = homeoCongr e.symm

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic
decls.doc:
Two maps `f g : C(X, Y)` are **ambient isotopic** if some ambient isotopy of the codomain `Y`
carries `f` to `g`, that is, its final homeomorphism postcomposes `f` to `g`. This is the
continuous topological ambient-isotopy relation intended to underlie later knot-equivalence
specialisations (ambient isotopy of smooth embeddings `S¹ ↪ M`); it does not itself encode the
smooth or PL structure those specialisations add.
decls.statement: def AmbientIsotopic (f g : C(X, Y)) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.ambientIsotopic_def
decls.doc:
`f` and `g` are ambient isotopic exactly when some ambient isotopy's final homeomorphism
postcomposes `f` to `g`; this restates the definition without unfolding it.
decls.statement:
theorem ambientIsotopic_def {f g : C(X, Y)} :
    AmbientIsotopic f g ↔ ∃ Φ : AmbientIsotopy Y, Φ.final.comp f = g

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.of_ambientIsotopy
decls.doc: An ambient isotopy carrying `f` to `g` witnesses that `f` and `g` are ambient isotopic.
decls.statement:
theorem of_ambientIsotopy (Φ : AmbientIsotopy Y) {f : C(X, Y)} :
    AmbientIsotopic f (Φ.final.comp f)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.refl
decls.doc: Ambient isotopy is reflexive: the constant ambient isotopy fixes every map.
decls.statement: theorem refl (f : C(X, Y)) : AmbientIsotopic f f

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.symm
decls.doc: Ambient isotopy is symmetric, via the inverse ambient isotopy.
decls.statement: theorem symm (hfg : AmbientIsotopic f g) : AmbientIsotopic g f

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.trans
decls.doc: Ambient isotopy is transitive, via the composite ambient isotopy.
decls.statement: theorem trans (hfg : AmbientIsotopic f g) (hgh : AmbientIsotopic g h) : AmbientIsotopic f h

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.isotopic
decls.doc:
Ambient isotopic embeddings are isotopic: this specialises the ambient relation to the general
isotopy relation, the "ambient isotopy implies isotopy" direction at the level of maps.
decls.statement: theorem isotopic (hfg : AmbientIsotopic f g) (hf : IsEmbedding f) : Isotopic f g

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.equivalence
decls.doc: Ambient isotopy is an equivalence relation on `C(X, Y)`.
decls.statement: theorem equivalence : Equivalence (AmbientIsotopic (X := X) (Y := Y))

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.setoid
decls.doc: The ambient-isotopy equivalence relation on `C(X, Y)`, packaged as a `Setoid`.
decls.statement:
def setoid (X Y : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] :
    Setoid (C(X, Y))

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.setoid_r_iff
decls.statement: theorem setoid_r_iff {f g : C(X, Y)} : (setoid X Y).r f g ↔ AmbientIsotopic f g

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.range_final_comp
decls.doc:
The final homeomorphism of an ambient isotopy carries `range f` onto the range of the moved
map `Φ.final.comp f`: the image `Φ.finalHomeomorph '' range f` is `range (Φ.final.comp f)`.
decls.statement:
theorem range_final_comp :
    Set.range (Φ.final.comp f) = Φ.finalHomeomorph '' Set.range f

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.mem_range_iff
decls.doc:
A point lies in `range f` exactly when its image under the final homeomorphism lies in the
range of the moved map. This is the compatibility that lets the final homeomorphism restrict to
the ranges (and, negated, to the complements).
decls.statement:
theorem mem_range_iff (y : Y) :
    y ∈ Set.range f ↔ Φ.finalHomeomorph y ∈ Set.range (Φ.final.comp f)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.notMem_range_iff
decls.doc:
A point misses `range f` exactly when its image under the final homeomorphism misses the range
of the moved map. This is the compatibility that lets the final homeomorphism restrict to the
complements.
decls.statement:
theorem notMem_range_iff (y : Y) :
    y ∉ Set.range f ↔ Φ.finalHomeomorph y ∉ Set.range (Φ.final.comp f)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.rangeHomeomorph
decls.doc:
The homeomorphism of ranges induced by an ambient isotopy: `Φ.finalHomeomorph` restricts to a
homeomorphism from `range f` onto the range of the moved map `Φ.final.comp f`.
decls.statement: def rangeHomeomorph : Set.range f ≃ₜ Set.range (Φ.final.comp f)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.coe_rangeHomeomorph_apply
decls.statement:
theorem coe_rangeHomeomorph_apply (y : Set.range f) :
    (Φ.rangeHomeomorph f y : Y) = Φ.finalHomeomorph y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.coe_rangeHomeomorph_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem coe_rangeHomeomorph_symm_apply (y : Set.range (Φ.final.comp f)) :
    ((Φ.rangeHomeomorph f).symm y : Y) = Φ.finalHomeomorph.symm y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.complementHomeomorph
decls.doc:
The homeomorphism of complements induced by an ambient isotopy: `Φ.finalHomeomorph` restricts
to a homeomorphism from `(range f)ᶜ` onto `(range (Φ.final.comp f))ᶜ`. This is the point-set core
of knot-complement invariance under ambient isotopy.
decls.statement:
def complementHomeomorph :
    ↥(Set.range f)ᶜ ≃ₜ ↥(Set.range (Φ.final.comp f))ᶜ

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.coe_complementHomeomorph_apply
decls.statement:
theorem coe_complementHomeomorph_apply (y : ↥(Set.range f)ᶜ) :
    (Φ.complementHomeomorph f y : Y) = Φ.finalHomeomorph y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.coe_complementHomeomorph_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem coe_complementHomeomorph_symm_apply (y : ↥(Set.range (Φ.final.comp f))ᶜ) :
    ((Φ.complementHomeomorph f).symm y : Y) = Φ.finalHomeomorph.symm y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.nonempty_rangeHomeomorph
decls.doc:
**Ambient isotopy preserves ranges up to homeomorphism.** If `f` and `g` are ambient isotopic,
their ranges (the embedded images, for embeddings) are homeomorphic.
decls.title: Ambient isotopy preserves ranges up to homeomorphism
decls.statement:
theorem nonempty_rangeHomeomorph (hfg : AmbientIsotopic f g) :
    Nonempty (Set.range f ≃ₜ Set.range g)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.nonempty_complementHomeomorph
decls.doc:
**Ambient isotopy preserves complements up to homeomorphism.** If `f` and `g` are ambient
isotopic, the complements `(range f)ᶜ` and `(range g)ᶜ` are homeomorphic. For knots (embeddings
`S¹ ↪ M`) this is the invariance of the knot complement, the reason knot invariants are built on
ambient isotopy rather than on the naive isotopy relation.
decls.title: Ambient isotopy preserves complements up to homeomorphism
decls.statement:
theorem nonempty_complementHomeomorph (hfg : AmbientIsotopic f g) :
    Nonempty (↥(Set.range f)ᶜ ≃ₜ ↥(Set.range g)ᶜ)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.precomp
decls.doc:
Ambient isotopy survives precomposition by any continuous source map. If an ambient isotopy
of `Y` carries `f` to `g`, the same ambient isotopy carries `f ∘ e` to `g ∘ e`.
decls.statement:
theorem precomp (hfg : AmbientIsotopic f g) (e : C(W, X)) :
    AmbientIsotopic (f.comp e) (g.comp e)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.postcomp_homeomorph
decls.doc:
Ambient isotopy survives postcomposition by a homeomorphism of ambient spaces. The witnessing
ambient isotopy is obtained by transporting the original one across the homeomorphism.
decls.statement:
theorem postcomp_homeomorph (hfg : AmbientIsotopic f g) (h : Y ≃ₜ Z) :
    AmbientIsotopic ((h : C(Y, Z)).comp f) ((h : C(Y, Z)).comp g)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.postcomp_homeomorph_precomp
decls.doc:
The two-sided coordinate-change form: precompose the source by any continuous map and
postcompose the ambient space by a homeomorphism.
decls.statement:
theorem postcomp_homeomorph_precomp (hfg : AmbientIsotopic f g) (h : Y ≃ₜ Z) (e : C(W, X)) :
    AmbientIsotopic ((h : C(Y, Z)).comp (f.comp e)) ((h : C(Y, Z)).comp (g.comp e))

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.transport
decls.doc:
**Transport of an ambient isotopy** across a homeomorphism `h : Y ≃ₜ Z` of ambient spaces:
at each time `t` run the homeomorphism `Φ t` in the coordinates supplied by `h`, giving
`z ↦ h (Φ (t, h⁻¹ z))`. The total map is a homeomorphism because it is `Φ`'s total homeomorphism
pre- and post-composed with the product homeomorphisms `id ×ₜ h⁻¹` and `id ×ₜ h`.
decls.title: Transport of an ambient isotopy
decls.statement: def transport (h : Y ≃ₜ Z) : AmbientIsotopy Z

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.transport_apply
decls.statement:
theorem transport_apply (h : Y ≃ₜ Z) (p : I × Z) :
    (Φ.transport h).toContinuousMap p = h (Φ.toContinuousMap (p.1, h.symm p.2))

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.final_transport
decls.statement:
theorem final_transport (h : Y ≃ₜ Z) (z : Z) :
    (Φ.transport h).final z = h (Φ.final (h.symm z))

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.homeomorph_transport
decls.doc:
Every time slice of a transported ambient isotopy is the corresponding slice of `Φ` read in
the coordinates supplied by `h`:
`(Φ.transport h).homeomorph t = (h.symm.trans (Φ.homeomorph t)).trans h`.
decls.statement:
theorem homeomorph_transport (h : Y ≃ₜ Z) (t : I) :
    (Φ.transport h).homeomorph t = (h.symm.trans (Φ.homeomorph t)).trans h

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.finalHomeomorph_transport
decls.doc:
The final homeomorphism of a transported ambient isotopy is the final homeomorphism of `Φ`
read in the coordinates supplied by `h`:
`(Φ.transport h).finalHomeomorph = (h.symm.trans Φ.finalHomeomorph).trans h`.
decls.statement:
theorem finalHomeomorph_transport (h : Y ≃ₜ Z) :
    (Φ.transport h).finalHomeomorph = (h.symm.trans Φ.finalHomeomorph).trans h

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.conj
decls.doc:
**Conjugation of an ambient isotopy** by a self-homeomorphism `h`: the special case of
`AmbientIsotopy.transport` in which the change of coordinates fixes the ambient space, so the
endpoint slices conjugate inside the group `Y ≃ₜ Y`. The total map is
`(t, y) ↦ (t, h (Φ (t, h⁻¹ y)))`.
decls.title: Conjugation of an ambient isotopy
decls.statement: def conj (h : Y ≃ₜ Y) : AmbientIsotopy Y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.conj_apply
decls.statement:
theorem conj_apply (h : Y ≃ₜ Y) (p : I × Y) :
    (Φ.conj h).toContinuousMap p = h (Φ.toContinuousMap (p.1, h.symm p.2))

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.final_conj
decls.statement: theorem final_conj (h : Y ≃ₜ Y) (y : Y) : (Φ.conj h).final y = h (Φ.final (h.symm y))

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.homeomorph_conj
decls.doc:
Every time slice of a conjugated ambient isotopy is the conjugate of the corresponding time
slice: `(Φ.conj h).homeomorph t = h * Φ.homeomorph t * h⁻¹`.
decls.statement:
theorem homeomorph_conj (h : Y ≃ₜ Y) (t : I) :
    (Φ.conj h).homeomorph t = h * Φ.homeomorph t * h⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.finalHomeomorph_conj
decls.doc:
The final homeomorphism of a conjugated ambient isotopy is the conjugate of the final
homeomorphism: `(Φ.conj h).finalHomeomorph = h * Φ.finalHomeomorph * h⁻¹`.
decls.statement:
theorem finalHomeomorph_conj (h : Y ≃ₜ Y) :
    (Φ.conj h).finalHomeomorph = h * Φ.finalHomeomorph * h⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.map_injective
decls.doc:
A covering map induces an injective map on fundamental groups. This is the fundamental-group
form of Mathlib's `IsCoveringMap.injective_path_homotopic_map`, which states the same injectivity
for every Hom-set of the fundamental groupoid.
decls.statement:
theorem IsCoveringMap.map_injective (hp : _root_.IsCoveringMap p) (e : E) :
    Function.Injective (_root_.FundamentalGroup.map ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ e)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.mapOfEq_injective
decls.doc:
A covering map induces an injective map on fundamental groups, in the form transported along
an equality `p e = x` of basepoints.

Combined with `MonoidHom.ofInjective`, this exhibits the image subgroup `p_* π₁(E, e)` as a copy
of `π₁(E, e)`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsCoveringMap.mapOfEq_injective (hp : _root_.IsCoveringMap p) {e : E} (he : p e = x) :
    Function.Injective (_root_.FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ he)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts_of_range_le_subgroup
decls.doc:
The lifting criterion for a covering map, with the subgroup inclusion factored through an
intermediate subgroup `H ≤ π₁(X, f a₀)`.

This is the form used when a cover is known to have recovered subgroup `H`: to lift `f`, it
suffices to show that `f_* π₁(A, a₀)` lies in `H`, and that `H` is contained in the image of
`p_* π₁(E, e₀)`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsCoveringMap.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts_of_range_le_subgroup
    (hp : _root_.IsCoveringMap p) [PathConnectedSpace A] [LocallyPathConnectedSpace A]
    {f : C(A, X)} {a₀ : A} {e₀ : E} (he : p e₀ = f a₀)
    (H : Subgroup (_root_.FundamentalGroup X (f a₀)))
    (hfH : (_root_.FundamentalGroup.map f a₀).range ≤ H)
    (hHp : H ≤ (_root_.FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ he).range) :
    ∃! F : C(A, E), F a₀ = e₀ ∧ p ∘ F = f

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts_of_subsingleton_fundamentalGroup
decls.doc:
The lifting criterion when the source fundamental group at `a₀` is subsingleton. In this
case the induced subgroup `f_* π₁(A, a₀)` is trivial.
decls.statement:
theorem IsCoveringMap.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts_of_subsingleton_fundamentalGroup
    (hp : _root_.IsCoveringMap p) [PathConnectedSpace A] [LocallyPathConnectedSpace A]
    {f : C(A, X)} {a₀ : A} {e₀ : E}
    [Subsingleton (_root_.FundamentalGroup A a₀)] (he : p e₀ = f a₀) :
    ∃! F : C(A, E), F a₀ = e₀ ∧ p ∘ F = f

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber
decls.doc:
Choosing a basepoint lift `e` in the fibre over `x` identifies the fundamental group of
the base with that fibre, via `γ ↦ monodromy γ e`.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber_apply_coe
decls.doc:
The general fibre equivalence sends a loop class to the monodromy translate of the chosen
lift, as an equality in the total space `E`.
decls.statement:
lemma IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber_apply_coe [SimplyConnectedSpace E]
    (hp : IsCoveringMap p) (e : p ⁻¹' {x}) (γ : FundamentalGroup X x) :
    (IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber hp e γ : E) = (hp.monodromy γ e : E)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber_apply
decls.doc:
The general fibre equivalence sends a loop class to the monodromy translate of the chosen
lift, as an equality in the fibre subtype.
decls.statement:
lemma IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber_apply [SimplyConnectedSpace E]
    (hp : IsCoveringMap p) (e : p ⁻¹' {x}) (γ : FundamentalGroup X x) :
    IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber hp e γ = hp.monodromy γ e

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber_apply_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse of the general fibre equivalence is characterized by the loop class whose
monodromy sends the chosen lift to the requested fibre point.
decls.statement:
lemma IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber_apply_symm_apply [SimplyConnectedSpace E]
    (hp : IsCoveringMap p) (e e' : p ⁻¹' {x}) :
    hp.monodromy ((IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber hp e).symm e') e = e'

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber_apply_symm_apply_coe
decls.doc:
On underlying points, the inverse of the general fibre equivalence is characterized by
the loop class whose monodromy sends the chosen lift to the requested fibre point.
decls.statement:
lemma IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber_apply_symm_apply_coe [SimplyConnectedSpace E]
    (hp : IsCoveringMap p) (e e' : p ⁻¹' {x}) :
    (hp.monodromy ((IsCoveringMap.fundamentalGroupEquivFiber hp e).symm e') e : E) = e'

decls.name: TauCeti.pathTowardZero
decls.doc:
The straight-line path in the unit interval `I` from `a` to `0`, given by `t ↦ a * σ t`
where `σ` is the interval symmetry `t ↦ 1 - t`.
decls.statement: def pathTowardZero (a : I) : Path a 0

decls.name: TauCeti.pathTowardZero_apply
decls.statement: theorem pathTowardZero_apply (a t : I) : pathTowardZero a t = a * σ t

decls.name: TauCeti.isPathConnected_cube
decls.doc:
The cube `I^N` is path connected: every point is joined to the corner `0` by the pointwise
product of the coordinate paths `pathTowardZero`.
decls.statement: theorem isPathConnected_cube : IsPathConnected (Set.univ : Set (I^N))

decls.name: TauCeti.zero_mem_cubeBoundary
decls.doc: The corner `0` lies on the boundary of the cube (any coordinate is `0`).
decls.statement: theorem zero_mem_cubeBoundary [Nonempty N] : (0 : I^N) ∈ Cube.boundary N

decls.name: TauCeti.cubeCollapseComplement
decls.doc:
The path in `I^N` dragging every coordinate other than `i₀` to `0`, while holding the
`i₀`-coordinate fixed at `y i₀`. Its endpoint is supported on `i₀`.
decls.statement:
def cubeCollapseComplement (i₀ : N) (y : I^N) :
    Path y (Function.update (0 : I^N) i₀ (y i₀))

decls.name: TauCeti.cubeCollapseComplement_apply
decls.statement:
theorem cubeCollapseComplement_apply (i₀ : N) (y : I^N) (t : I) :
    cubeCollapseComplement i₀ y t
      = Function.update (fun j => pathTowardZero (y j) t) i₀ (y i₀)

decls.name: TauCeti.cubeCollapseCoord
decls.doc:
The path in `I^N` dragging the `i₀`-coordinate from `a` to `0`, with every other
coordinate held at `0`. It runs from the point supported on `i₀` back to the corner `0`.
decls.statement: def cubeCollapseCoord (i₀ : N) (a : I) : Path (Function.update (0 : I^N) i₀ a) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.cubeCollapseCoord_apply
decls.statement:
theorem cubeCollapseCoord_apply (i₀ : N) (a t : I) :
    cubeCollapseCoord i₀ a t = Function.update (0 : I^N) i₀ (pathTowardZero a t)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPathConnected_cubeBoundary
decls.doc:
The boundary of the cube `I^N` is path connected once the index type has at least two
elements. Any boundary point `y`, extreme in some coordinate `i₀`, is joined to the corner `0`
in two phases: first collapse every other coordinate to `0` (keeping `i₀` extreme), then
collapse the `i₀`-coordinate (keeping a *different* coordinate `j₀` at `0`). The two-element
hypothesis provides the index `j₀ ≠ i₀`.
decls.statement: theorem isPathConnected_cubeBoundary [Nontrivial N] : IsPathConnected (Cube.boundary N)

decls.name: TauCeti.isConnected_cubeBoundary
decls.doc: The boundary of the cube `I^N` is connected once the index type has at least two elements.
decls.statement: theorem isConnected_cubeBoundary [Nontrivial N] : IsConnected (Cube.boundary N)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPreconnected_cubeBoundary
decls.doc:
The boundary of the cube `I^N` is preconnected once the index type has at least two
elements.
decls.statement: theorem isPreconnected_cubeBoundary [Nontrivial N] : IsPreconnected (Cube.boundary N)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPathConnected_cubeBoundary_fin
decls.doc:
The boundary of the `n`-cube `I^(Fin n)` is path connected for `2 ≤ n`. This is the shape
in which the connectivity feeds into `π_ n` for `n ≥ 2`.
decls.statement:
theorem isPathConnected_cubeBoundary_fin {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    IsPathConnected (Cube.boundary (Fin n))

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_homotopic_iff
decls.doc:
Postcomposition with a covering map `p` neither creates nor destroys homotopies between
generalized loops in the total space: two generalized loops based at `e` are homotopic
relative to the cube boundary if and only if their postcompositions with `p` are.

The reverse implication is `TauCeti.GenLoop.map_homotopic` and needs no hypothesis on `p`;
the forward implication lifts the homotopy, using that both generalized loops take the value
`e` at the corner `0` of the cube.
decls.statement:
theorem map_homotopic_iff [Nonempty N] (hp : IsCoveringMap p) {F G : Ω^ N E e} :
    _root_.GenLoop.Homotopic (map ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ rfl F) (map ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ rfl G) ↔
      _root_.GenLoop.Homotopic F G

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_surjective
decls.doc:
Every generalized loop in the base of a covering map lifts, in dimensions `≥ 2`, to a
generalized loop in the total space based at any prescribed point `e` of the fibre.

The index type is assumed nontrivial (equivalently: the dimension is at least `2`), so after
splitting off one coordinate there is another coordinate whose boundary can be held fixed by a
relative homotopy lift. In dimension `1` the statement is false: a loop in the base lifts to a
*path* in the total space, whose endpoint need not return to `e`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_surjective [Nontrivial N] (hp : IsCoveringMap p) (f : Ω^ N X (p e)) :
    ∃ F : Ω^ N E e, map ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ rfl F = f

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_injective
decls.doc: A covering map is injective on homotopy groups in every positive dimension.
decls.statement:
theorem map_injective [Nonempty N] (hp : IsCoveringMap p) :
    Function.Injective (map (N := N) (⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ : C(E, X)) (rfl : p e = p e))

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_surjective
decls.doc: A covering map is surjective on homotopy groups in dimensions `≥ 2`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_surjective [Nontrivial N] (hp : IsCoveringMap p) :
    Function.Surjective (map (N := N) (⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ : C(E, X)) (rfl : p e = p e))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.homotopyGroupMulEquiv
decls.doc:
**A covering map induces an isomorphism on homotopy groups in dimensions `≥ 2`.**

Postcomposition with `p` is a group isomorphism `π_N(E, e) ≃* π_N(X, p e)` whenever the index
type `N` has at least two elements. No connectivity hypothesis on `E` or `X` is needed: both
halves are statements about lifting cubes.
decls.title: A covering map induces an isomorphism on homotopy groups in dimensions `≥ 2`
decls.statement:
def IsCoveringMap.homotopyGroupMulEquiv [DecidableEq N] [Nontrivial N]
    (hp : _root_.IsCoveringMap p) (e : E) :
    HomotopyGroup N E e ≃* HomotopyGroup N X (p e)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.homotopyGroupMulEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem IsCoveringMap.homotopyGroupMulEquiv_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nontrivial N]
    (hp : _root_.IsCoveringMap p) (e : E) (a : HomotopyGroup N E e) :
    IsCoveringMap.homotopyGroupMulEquiv hp e a =
      HomotopyGroup.map (⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ : C(E, X)) rfl a

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.homotopyGroupPiMulEquiv
decls.doc:
The `π_(n + 2)` form of `TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.homotopyGroupMulEquiv`: a covering map
`p : E → X` induces `π_(n + 2)(E, e) ≃* π_(n + 2)(X, p e)` for every `n : ℕ`.
decls.statement:
def IsCoveringMap.homotopyGroupPiMulEquiv (hp : _root_.IsCoveringMap p)
    (e : E) (n : ℕ) : π_ (n + 2) E e ≃* π_ (n + 2) X (p e)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.homotopyGroupPiMulEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem IsCoveringMap.homotopyGroupPiMulEquiv_apply (hp : _root_.IsCoveringMap p) (e : E)
    (n : ℕ) (a : π_ (n + 2) E e) :
    IsCoveringMap.homotopyGroupPiMulEquiv hp e n a =
      HomotopyGroup.map (⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ : C(E, X)) rfl a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphEquivOfEq
decls.doc:
A homeomorphism `e : X ≃ₜ Y` carrying `x` to `y` induces an equivalence of homotopy groups
`π_N(X, x) ≃ π_N(Y, y)`. The forward map is `HomotopyGroup.map` of `e`; the inverse is
`HomotopyGroup.map` of `e.symm`. This holds in every dimension `N`.
decls.statement:
def homeomorphEquivOfEq (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (h : e x = y) :
    HomotopyGroup N X x ≃ HomotopyGroup N Y y

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphEquivOfEq_apply
decls.statement:
theorem homeomorphEquivOfEq_apply (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (h : e x = y) (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    homeomorphEquivOfEq e h a = map ⟨e, e.continuous⟩ h a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphEquivOfEq_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem homeomorphEquivOfEq_symm_apply (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (h : e x = y) (b : HomotopyGroup N Y y) :
    (homeomorphEquivOfEq e h).symm b =
      map ⟨e.symm, e.symm.continuous⟩ (e.symm_apply_eq.mpr h.symm) b

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphEquiv
decls.doc:
A homeomorphism `e : X ≃ₜ Y` induces an equivalence of homotopy groups
`π_N(X, x) ≃ π_N(Y, e x)`, in every dimension `N`.
decls.statement:
def homeomorphEquiv (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (x : X) :
    HomotopyGroup N X x ≃ HomotopyGroup N Y (e x)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem homeomorphEquiv_apply (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (x : X) (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    homeomorphEquiv e x a = map ⟨e, e.continuous⟩ rfl a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem homeomorphEquiv_symm_apply (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (x : X) (b : HomotopyGroup N Y (e x)) :
    (homeomorphEquiv e x).symm b =
      map ⟨e.symm, e.symm.continuous⟩ (e.symm_apply_apply x) b

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphMulEquivOfEq
decls.doc:
A homeomorphism `e : X ≃ₜ Y` carrying `x` to `y` induces an isomorphism of homotopy groups
`π_N(X, x) ≃* π_N(Y, y)` in positive dimensions.
decls.statement:
def homeomorphMulEquivOfEq [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N]
    (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (h : e x = y) :
    HomotopyGroup N X x ≃* HomotopyGroup N Y y

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphMulEquivOfEq_apply
decls.statement:
theorem homeomorphMulEquivOfEq_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (h : e x = y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    homeomorphMulEquivOfEq e h a = map ⟨e, e.continuous⟩ h a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphMulEquivOfEq_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem homeomorphMulEquivOfEq_symm_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (h : e x = y)
    (b : HomotopyGroup N Y y) :
    (homeomorphMulEquivOfEq e h).symm b =
      map ⟨e.symm, e.symm.continuous⟩ (e.symm_apply_eq.mpr h.symm) b

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphMulEquiv
decls.doc:
A homeomorphism `e : X ≃ₜ Y` induces an isomorphism of homotopy groups
`π_N(X, x) ≃* π_N(Y, e x)` in positive dimensions.
decls.statement:
def homeomorphMulEquiv [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (x : X) :
    HomotopyGroup N X x ≃* HomotopyGroup N Y (e x)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphMulEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem homeomorphMulEquiv_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (x : X)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    homeomorphMulEquiv e x a = map ⟨e, e.continuous⟩ rfl a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphMulEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem homeomorphMulEquiv_symm_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (x : X)
    (b : HomotopyGroup N Y (e x)) :
    (homeomorphMulEquiv e x).symm b =
      map ⟨e.symm, e.symm.continuous⟩ (e.symm_apply_apply x) b

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_homotopic_of_homotopicRel
decls.doc:
Postcomposing a generalized loop with maps homotopic relative to a set containing the
basepoint gives homotopic generalized loops. The resulting homotopy is relative to the cube
boundary.

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_eq_of_homotopicRel
decls.doc:
Continuous maps homotopic relative to a set containing the basepoint induce the same
function on homotopy groups.

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom_eq_of_homotopicRel
decls.doc:
Continuous maps homotopic relative to a set containing the basepoint have equal induced
monoid homomorphisms on positive-dimensional homotopy groups.

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map
decls.doc: A based continuous map sends generalized loops to generalized loops by postcomposition.
decls.statement: def map (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) (p : Ω^ N X x) : Ω^ N Y y

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_apply
decls.statement:
theorem map_apply (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) (p : Ω^ N X x) (t : I^N) :
    map f hf p t = f (p t)

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_const
decls.statement:
theorem map_const (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) :
    map f hf (_root_.GenLoop.const : Ω^ N X x) =
      (_root_.GenLoop.const : Ω^ N Y y)

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_continuousMap_const
decls.doc:
Postcomposition by a constant continuous map gives the constant generalized loop.

This is not a `simp` lemma: baking the basepoint proof `rfl` into the statement forces the
target basepoint to be `(ContinuousMap.const X y) x` rather than `y`, so `simp` cannot close
even its own statement. Use it as an explicit rewrite.
decls.statement:
theorem map_continuousMap_const (y : Y) (p : Ω^ N X x) :
    map (ContinuousMap.const X y) rfl p = (_root_.GenLoop.const : Ω^ N Y y)

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_id
decls.statement:
theorem map_id (p : Ω^ N X x) :
    map (ContinuousMap.id X) rfl p = p

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_comp
decls.statement:
theorem map_comp (g : C(Y, Z)) (hg : g y = z) (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y)
    (p : Ω^ N X x) :
    map g hg (map f hf p) = map (g.comp f) (by simp [hf, hg]) p

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_homotopic
decls.doc: Postcomposition preserves homotopy relative to the cube boundary.
decls.statement:
theorem map_homotopic {f g : Ω^ N X x} (h : _root_.GenLoop.Homotopic f g)
    (F : C(X, Y)) (hF : F x = y) :
    _root_.GenLoop.Homotopic (map F hF f) (map F hF g)

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_transAt
decls.statement:
theorem map_transAt (F : C(X, Y)) (hF : F x = y) (i : N) (p q : Ω^ N X x) :
    map F hF (_root_.GenLoop.transAt i p q) =
      _root_.GenLoop.transAt i (map F hF p) (map F hF q)

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_symmAt
decls.statement:
theorem map_symmAt (F : C(X, Y)) (hF : F x = y) (i : N) (p : Ω^ N X x) :
    map F hF (_root_.GenLoop.symmAt i p) =
      _root_.GenLoop.symmAt i (map F hF p)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mk_const_eq_one
decls.doc:
In positive dimensions, the class of the constant generalized loop is the identity element.
This is `HomotopyGroup.one_def` oriented towards `1`, so that `1` is the simp normal form for
the constant-map results below.
decls.statement:
theorem mk_const_eq_one [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] :
    (⟦(_root_.GenLoop.const : Ω^ N X x)⟧ : HomotopyGroup N X x) = (1 : HomotopyGroup N X x)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map
decls.doc: The map on homotopy classes induced by a based continuous map.
decls.statement:
def map (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) :
    HomotopyGroup N X x → HomotopyGroup N Y y

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_mk
decls.statement:
theorem map_mk (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) (p : Ω^ N X x) :
    map f hf (⟦p⟧ : HomotopyGroup N X x) = ⟦GenLoop.map f hf p⟧

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_continuousMap_const_apply
decls.doc:
A constant continuous map sends every homotopy class to the class of the constant
generalized loop. This statement also covers dimension zero, where the target need not carry
the positive-dimensional group structure.
decls.statement:
theorem map_continuousMap_const_apply (y : Y) (hy : (ContinuousMap.const X y) x = y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map (x := x) (ContinuousMap.const X y) hy a =
      (⟦(_root_.GenLoop.const : Ω^ N Y y)⟧ : HomotopyGroup N Y y)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_eq_continuousMap_const_of_subsingleton
decls.doc:
A based map into a subsingleton space induces the same map as the constant map at the
target basepoint.
decls.statement:
theorem map_eq_continuousMap_const_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton Y]
    (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) :
    map (N := N) f hf = map (x := x) (ContinuousMap.const X y) rfl

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_apply_of_subsingleton
decls.doc:
A based map into a subsingleton space sends every homotopy class to the class of the
constant generalized loop.
decls.statement:
theorem map_apply_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton Y] (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map (N := N) f hf a =
      (⟦(_root_.GenLoop.const : Ω^ N Y y)⟧ : HomotopyGroup N Y y)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_continuousMap_const_apply_eq_one
decls.doc:
In positive dimensions, a constant continuous map sends every homotopy class to the
identity.

This is not a `simp` lemma: the positive-dimensional normal form is already reached by
`map_continuousMap_const_apply` followed by `mk_const_eq_one`, so a separate `⟦const⟧`-keyed
`= 1` rule would be redundant. It is kept as an explicit rewrite.
decls.statement:
theorem map_continuousMap_const_apply_eq_one [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N]
    (y : Y) (hy : (ContinuousMap.const X y) x = y) (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map (x := x) (ContinuousMap.const X y) hy a = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_apply_eq_one_of_subsingleton
decls.doc:
In positive dimensions, a based map into a subsingleton space sends every homotopy class
to the identity.

This is not a `simp` lemma: the positive-dimensional normal form is already reached by
`map_apply_of_subsingleton` followed by `mk_const_eq_one`, so a separate composite `= 1` rule
would be redundant. It is kept as an explicit rewrite.
decls.statement:
theorem map_apply_eq_one_of_subsingleton [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] [Subsingleton Y]
    (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map (N := N) f hf a = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_id_apply
decls.doc:
Identity law: the map induced by the identity continuous map is the identity on homotopy
classes.
decls.statement:
theorem map_id_apply (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map (ContinuousMap.id X) rfl a = a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_comp_apply
decls.doc:
Composition law: the map induced by a composite continuous map is the composite of the
induced maps on homotopy classes.
decls.statement:
theorem map_comp_apply (g : C(Y, Z)) (hg : g y = z) (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map g hg (map f hf a) = map (g.comp f) (by simp [hf, hg]) a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_congr
decls.doc:
The induced map `HomotopyGroup.map` depends only on the underlying continuous map, not on the
chosen proof of the basepoint equation.
decls.statement:
theorem map_congr {f₁ f₂ : C(X, Y)} (hfe : f₁ = f₂) (h₁ : f₁ x = y) (h₂ : f₂ x = y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map f₁ h₁ a = map f₂ h₂ a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_map_of_comp_eq_id
decls.doc:
If `g ∘ f` is the identity, then the induced map of `g` undoes the induced map of `f` on
homotopy classes.
decls.statement:
theorem map_map_of_comp_eq_id (g : C(Y, X)) (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) (hg : g y = x)
    (hgf : g.comp f = ContinuousMap.id X) (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map g hg (map f hf a) = a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom
decls.doc:
In positive dimensions, the map induced by a based continuous map is a monoid
homomorphism for the standard group structure on homotopy groups.
decls.statement:
def mapHom [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) :
    HomotopyGroup N X x →* HomotopyGroup N Y y

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom_apply
decls.statement:
theorem mapHom_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    mapHom f hf a = map f hf a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom_continuousMap_const_eq_one
decls.doc:
In positive dimensions, a constant continuous map induces the trivial homomorphism on
homotopy groups.

This is not a `simp` lemma: baking the basepoint proof `rfl` into the statement forces the
target basepoint to be `(ContinuousMap.const X y) x` rather than `y`, so `simp` cannot close
even its own statement. Use it as an explicit rewrite.
decls.statement:
theorem mapHom_continuousMap_const_eq_one [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (y : Y) :
    mapHom (N := N) (x := x) (ContinuousMap.const X y) rfl = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom_eq_one_of_subsingleton
decls.doc:
A based map into a subsingleton space induces the trivial homomorphism on every
positive-dimensional homotopy group.
decls.statement:
theorem mapHom_eq_one_of_subsingleton [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] [Subsingleton Y]
    (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) : mapHom (N := N) f hf = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom_id
decls.doc:
Identity law for the bundled homomorphism: the induced monoid homomorphism of the identity
continuous map is the identity homomorphism.
decls.statement:
theorem mapHom_id [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] :
    mapHom (ContinuousMap.id X) rfl = MonoidHom.id (HomotopyGroup N X x)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom_comp
decls.doc:
Composition law for the bundled homomorphism: the induced monoid homomorphism of a composite
continuous map is the composite of the induced homomorphisms.
decls.statement:
theorem mapHom_comp [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (g : C(Y, Z)) (hg : g y = z)
    (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) :
    (mapHom g hg).comp (mapHom f hf) = mapHom (N := N) (g.comp f) (by simp [hf, hg])

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_mul
decls.statement:
theorem map_mul [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y)
    (a b : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map f hf (a * b) = map f hf a * map f hf b

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_one
decls.statement:
theorem map_one [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) :
    map f hf (1 : HomotopyGroup N X x) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.prod
decls.doc: The coordinatewise product of two generalized loops.
decls.statement: def prod (p : Ω^ N X x) (q : Ω^ N Y y) : Ω^ N (X × Y) (x, y)

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.prod_apply
decls.statement:
theorem prod_apply (p : Ω^ N X x) (q : Ω^ N Y y) (t : I^N) :
    prod p q t = (p t, q t)

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_fst_prod
decls.doc: Taking the first coordinate of a product generalized loop recovers the first loop.
decls.statement:
theorem map_fst_prod (p : Ω^ N X x) (q : Ω^ N Y y) :
    map (ContinuousMap.fst : C(X × Y, X)) rfl (prod p q) = p

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_snd_prod
decls.doc: Taking the second coordinate of a product generalized loop recovers the second loop.
decls.statement:
theorem map_snd_prod (p : Ω^ N X x) (q : Ω^ N Y y) :
    map (ContinuousMap.snd : C(X × Y, Y)) rfl (prod p q) = q

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.prod_map_fst_map_snd
decls.doc: A generalized loop in a product is recovered from its two coordinate loops.
decls.statement:
theorem prod_map_fst_map_snd (p : Ω^ N (X × Y) (x, y)) :
    prod (map (ContinuousMap.fst : C(X × Y, X)) rfl p)
      (map (ContinuousMap.snd : C(X × Y, Y)) rfl p) = p

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.prod_homotopic
decls.doc: Coordinatewise products preserve homotopy relative to the cube boundary.

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.pi
decls.doc: The coordinatewise indexed product of generalized loops.
decls.statement: def pi (p : ∀ i, Ω^ N (Z i) (z i)) : Ω^ N (∀ i, Z i) z

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.pi_apply
decls.statement:
theorem pi_apply (p : ∀ i, Ω^ N (Z i) (z i)) (t : I^N) (i : ι) :
    pi p t i = p i t

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.map_eval_pi
decls.doc: Taking a coordinate of an indexed product generalized loop recovers that coordinate loop.
decls.statement:
theorem map_eval_pi (p : ∀ i, Ω^ N (Z i) (z i)) (i : ι) :
    map (ContinuousMap.eval i) rfl (pi p) = p i

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.pi_map_eval
decls.doc: A generalized loop in an indexed product is recovered from all of its coordinate loops.
decls.statement:
theorem pi_map_eval (p : Ω^ N (∀ i, Z i) z) :
    pi (fun i ↦ map (ContinuousMap.eval i) rfl p) = p

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.pi_homotopic
decls.doc: Indexed products preserve coordinatewise homotopy relative to the cube boundary.

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.prod
decls.doc:
The product of two homotopy classes, represented by the coordinatewise product of
generalized loops.
decls.statement:
def prod (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) (b : HomotopyGroup N Y y) :
    HomotopyGroup N (X × Y) (x, y)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.prod_mk
decls.statement:
theorem prod_mk (p : Ω^ N X x) (q : Ω^ N Y y) :
    prod (⟦p⟧ : HomotopyGroup N X x) (⟦q⟧ : HomotopyGroup N Y y) =
      (⟦GenLoop.prod p q⟧ : HomotopyGroup N (X × Y) (x, y))

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_fst_prod
decls.doc: The first-coordinate map sends a product of homotopy classes to its first factor.
decls.statement:
theorem map_fst_prod (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) (b : HomotopyGroup N Y y) :
    map (ContinuousMap.fst : C(X × Y, X)) rfl (prod a b) = a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_snd_prod
decls.doc: The second-coordinate map sends a product of homotopy classes to its second factor.
decls.statement:
theorem map_snd_prod (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) (b : HomotopyGroup N Y y) :
    map (ContinuousMap.snd : C(X × Y, Y)) rfl (prod a b) = b

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.prod_map_fst_map_snd
decls.doc: A homotopy class in a product is recovered from its two coordinate classes.
decls.statement:
theorem prod_map_fst_map_snd (a : HomotopyGroup N (X × Y) (x, y)) :
    prod (map (ContinuousMap.fst : C(X × Y, X)) rfl a)
      (map (ContinuousMap.snd : C(X × Y, Y)) rfl a) = a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.prodEquiv
decls.doc: The homotopy group of a binary product is the product of the homotopy groups.

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.prodEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem prodEquiv_apply (x : X) (y : Y) (a : HomotopyGroup N (X × Y) (x, y)) :
    prodEquiv x y a =
      (map (ContinuousMap.fst : C(X × Y, X)) rfl a,
        map (ContinuousMap.snd : C(X × Y, Y)) rfl a)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.prodEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem prodEquiv_symm_apply (x : X) (y : Y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x × HomotopyGroup N Y y) :
    (prodEquiv x y).symm a = prod a.1 a.2

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.prodMulEquiv
decls.doc:
In positive dimensions, the homotopy group of a binary product is multiplicatively
equivalent to the product of the homotopy groups.

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.prodMulEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem prodMulEquiv_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (x : X) (y : Y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N (X × Y) (x, y)) :
    prodMulEquiv x y a = prodEquiv x y a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.prodMulEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem prodMulEquiv_symm_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (x : X) (y : Y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x × HomotopyGroup N Y y) :
    (prodMulEquiv x y).symm a = prod a.1 a.2

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.prod_one
decls.doc: The coordinatewise product of identity homotopy classes is the identity.
decls.statement:
theorem prod_one [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] :
    prod (1 : HomotopyGroup N X x) (1 : HomotopyGroup N Y y) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.prod_mul
decls.doc: Coordinatewise products commute with multiplication of homotopy classes.
decls.statement:
theorem prod_mul [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N]
    (a₁ a₂ : HomotopyGroup N X x) (b₁ b₂ : HomotopyGroup N Y y) :
    prod (a₁ * a₂) (b₁ * b₂) = prod a₁ b₁ * prod a₂ b₂

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.pi
decls.doc:
The indexed product of homotopy classes, represented by the coordinatewise product of
generalized loops.
decls.statement:
def pi (a : ∀ i, HomotopyGroup N (Z i) (z i)) :
    HomotopyGroup N (∀ i, Z i) z

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.pi_mk
decls.statement:
theorem pi_mk (p : ∀ i, Ω^ N (Z i) (z i)) :
    pi (fun i ↦ (⟦p i⟧ : HomotopyGroup N (Z i) (z i))) =
      (⟦GenLoop.pi p⟧ : HomotopyGroup N (∀ i, Z i) z)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_eval_pi
decls.doc: Taking a coordinate of an indexed product of homotopy classes recovers that coordinate.
decls.statement:
theorem map_eval_pi (a : ∀ i, HomotopyGroup N (Z i) (z i)) (i : ι) :
    map (ContinuousMap.eval i) rfl (pi a) = a i

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.pi_map_eval
decls.doc: A homotopy class in an indexed product is recovered from all of its coordinate classes.
decls.statement:
theorem pi_map_eval (a : HomotopyGroup N (∀ i, Z i) z) :
    pi (fun i ↦ map (ContinuousMap.eval i) rfl a) = a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.piEquiv
decls.doc: The homotopy group of an indexed product is the indexed product of the homotopy groups.
decls.statement:
def piEquiv (z : ∀ i, Z i) :
    HomotopyGroup N (∀ i, Z i) z ≃ ∀ i, HomotopyGroup N (Z i) (z i)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.piEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem piEquiv_apply (z : ∀ i, Z i) (a : HomotopyGroup N (∀ i, Z i) z) (i : ι) :
    piEquiv z a i = map (ContinuousMap.eval i) rfl a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.piEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem piEquiv_symm_apply (z : ∀ i, Z i)
    (a : ∀ i, HomotopyGroup N (Z i) (z i)) :
    (piEquiv z).symm a = pi a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.subsingleton_pi
decls.doc:
The homotopy group of an indexed product is a subsingleton when every factor homotopy
group is a subsingleton.
decls.statement:
instance subsingleton_pi [∀ i, Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup N (Z i) (z i))] :
    Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup N (∀ i, Z i) z)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.piMulEquiv
decls.doc:
In positive dimensions, the homotopy group of an indexed product is multiplicatively
equivalent to the indexed product of the homotopy groups.
decls.statement:
def piMulEquiv [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (z : ∀ i, Z i) :
    HomotopyGroup N (∀ i, Z i) z ≃* ∀ i, HomotopyGroup N (Z i) (z i)

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.piMulEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem piMulEquiv_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (z : ∀ i, Z i)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N (∀ i, Z i) z) (i : ι) :
    piMulEquiv z a i = map (ContinuousMap.eval i) rfl a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.piMulEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem piMulEquiv_symm_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (z : ∀ i, Z i)
    (a : ∀ i, HomotopyGroup N (Z i) (z i)) :
    (piMulEquiv z).symm a = pi a

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.pi_one
decls.doc: The coordinatewise indexed product of identity homotopy classes is the identity.
decls.statement:
theorem pi_one [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] :
    pi (fun _ ↦ 1 : ∀ i, HomotopyGroup N (Z i) (z i)) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.pi_mul
decls.doc: Coordinatewise indexed products commute with multiplication of homotopy classes.
decls.statement:
theorem pi_mul [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N]
    (a b : ∀ i, HomotopyGroup N (Z i) (z i)) :
    pi (a * b) = pi a * pi b

decls.name: TauCeti.GenLoop.homotopic_of_topologicalVectorSpace
decls.doc:
Any two generalized loops based at the same point in a real topological vector space are
homotopic relative to the cube boundary. The homotopy is pointwise linear interpolation.
decls.statement:
theorem homotopic_of_topologicalVectorSpace (f g : Ω^ N E x) :
    _root_.GenLoop.Homotopic f g

decls.name: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.subsingleton_of_topologicalVectorSpace
decls.doc:
Every homotopy group of a real topological vector space is a subsingleton. This includes
dimension zero: a real topological vector space is path connected.
decls.statement: instance subsingleton_of_topologicalVectorSpace : Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup N E x)

decls.name: TauCeti.isEmbedding_const_prod
decls.statement: theorem isEmbedding_const_prod (t : I) : IsEmbedding fun x : X => (t, x)

decls.name: TauCeti.isInducing_of_isClosed_cover
decls.doc:
A map is inducing if its restrictions to the preimages of a closed cover of the codomain are
inducing. (The closedness of the cover in the *codomain* is what makes the gluing work, even
though the analogous statement for an arbitrary closed cover of the domain fails.)
decls.statement:
theorem isInducing_of_isClosed_cover {Z W : Type*} [TopologicalSpace Z]
    [TopologicalSpace W] {f : Z → W} (hf : Continuous f) {D₁ D₂ : Set W}
    (h₁ : IsClosed D₁) (h₂ : IsClosed D₂) (hcov : D₁ ∪ D₂ = Set.univ)
    (hi₁ : IsInducing ((f ⁻¹' D₁).restrict f)) (hi₂ : IsInducing ((f ⁻¹' D₂).restrict f)) :
    IsInducing f

decls.name: TauCeti.isInducing_restrict_of_embedding
decls.doc:
If `e` is an embedding parametrising the preimage `f ⁻¹' D` and `f ∘ e` is inducing, then the
restriction of `f` to `f ⁻¹' D` is inducing.
decls.statement:
theorem isInducing_restrict_of_embedding {Z W A : Type*} [TopologicalSpace Z]
    [TopologicalSpace W] [TopologicalSpace A] {f : Z → W} {D : Set W} {e : A → Z}
    (he : IsEmbedding e) (hrange : Set.range e = f ⁻¹' D) (hfe : IsInducing (f ∘ e)) :
    IsInducing ((f ⁻¹' D).restrict f)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy
decls.doc:
An **isotopy** between `f₀ f₁ : C(X, Y)` is a homotopy whose level-preserving total map
`I × X → I × Y` is a topological embedding.

As an equivalence this non-ambient relation is too coarse for classical knot theory: it need not
extend to a motion of the ambient space and therefore need not preserve knot complements. Use
`AmbientIsotopy`/`AmbientIsotopic` for knot equivalence; see the module docstring and the
Burde--Zieschang reference.
decls.statement: structure Isotopy (f₀ f₁ : C(X, Y)) extends Homotopy f₀ f₁

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.instFunLike
decls.statement: instance instFunLike : FunLike (Isotopy f₀ f₁) (I × X) Y

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.totalMap
decls.doc: The level-preserving total map of an isotopy.
decls.statement: def totalMap (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) : C(I × X, I × Y)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.totalMap_apply
decls.statement:
theorem totalMap_apply (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (p : I × X) :
    F.totalMap p = (p.1, F.toHomotopy p)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.apply_zero
decls.statement: theorem apply_zero (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (x : X) : F (0, x) = f₀ x

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.apply_one
decls.statement: theorem apply_one (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (x : X) : F (1, x) = f₁ x

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.isEmbedding_total
decls.doc: The level-preserving total map of an isotopy is a topological embedding.
decls.statement: theorem isEmbedding_total (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) : IsEmbedding F.totalMap

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.isEmbedding_apply
decls.doc: Every time-slice of an isotopy is a topological embedding.
decls.statement:
theorem isEmbedding_apply (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (t : I) :
    IsEmbedding fun x => F.toHomotopy (t, x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.toHomotopyWith
decls.doc: An isotopy is, in particular, a `HomotopyWith` whose slices are embeddings.
decls.statement:
def toHomotopyWith (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) :
    HomotopyWith f₀ f₁ fun g : C(X, Y) => IsEmbedding g

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.isEmbedding_left
decls.doc: The map an isotopy starts at is a topological embedding.
decls.statement: theorem isEmbedding_left (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) : IsEmbedding f₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.isEmbedding_right
decls.doc: The map an isotopy ends at is a topological embedding.
decls.statement: theorem isEmbedding_right (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) : IsEmbedding f₁

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.trans_toHomotopy_apply_of_le
decls.doc:
Value of the concatenated homotopy on the first half `[0, 1 / 2]`, with the time parameter
rescaled to `2 * t`.
decls.statement:
theorem trans_toHomotopy_apply_of_le (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (G : Isotopy f₁ f₂) {t : I} (x : X)
    (h : (t : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2) :
    (F.toHomotopy.trans G.toHomotopy) (t, x)
      = F.toHomotopy (⟨2 * t, (unitInterval.mul_pos_mem_iff zero_lt_two).2 ⟨t.2.1, h⟩⟩, x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.trans_toHomotopy_apply_of_not_le
decls.doc:
Value of the concatenated homotopy on the second half `[1 / 2, 1]`, with the time parameter
rescaled to `2 * t - 1`.
decls.statement:
theorem trans_toHomotopy_apply_of_not_le (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (G : Isotopy f₁ f₂) {t : I}
    (x : X)
    (h : ¬ (t : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2) :
    (F.toHomotopy.trans G.toHomotopy) (t, x)
      = G.toHomotopy
          (⟨2 * t - 1, unitInterval.two_mul_sub_one_mem_iff.2 ⟨(not_le.1 h).le, t.2.2⟩⟩, x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.half
decls.doc: Halving reparametrisation `s ↦ s / 2 : I → I`, with image the left half `[0, 1 / 2]`.
decls.statement: def half (s : I) : I

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.halfRight
decls.doc: Right-half reparametrisation `s ↦ s / 2 + 1 / 2 : I → I`, with image `[1 / 2, 1]`.
decls.statement: def halfRight (s : I) : I

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.coe_half
decls.statement: theorem coe_half (s : I) : (half s : ℝ) = (s : ℝ) / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.coe_halfRight
decls.statement: theorem coe_halfRight (s : I) : (halfRight s : ℝ) = (s : ℝ) / 2 + 1 / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.injective_half
decls.statement: theorem injective_half : Function.Injective half

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.injective_halfRight
decls.statement: theorem injective_halfRight : Function.Injective halfRight

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.half_left_inv
decls.statement:
theorem half_left_inv (t : I) (ht : (t : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2) :
    half (⟨2 * t, ⟨by linarith [t.2.1], by linarith [ht]⟩⟩ : I) = t

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.halfRight_right_inv
decls.statement:
theorem halfRight_right_inv (t : I) (ht : 1 / 2 ≤ (t : ℝ)) :
    halfRight (⟨2 * t - 1, ⟨by linarith [ht], by linarith [t.2.2]⟩⟩ : I) = t

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.isEmbedding_half
decls.statement: theorem isEmbedding_half : IsEmbedding half

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.isEmbedding_halfRight
decls.statement: theorem isEmbedding_halfRight : IsEmbedding halfRight

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.range_half
decls.statement: theorem range_half : Set.range half = {t : I | (t : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2}

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.range_halfRight
decls.statement: theorem range_halfRight : Set.range halfRight = {t : I | 1 / 2 ≤ (t : ℝ)}

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.trans_half
decls.statement:
theorem trans_half (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (G : Isotopy f₁ f₂) (s : I) (x : X) :
    (F.toHomotopy.trans G.toHomotopy) (half s, x) = F.toHomotopy (s, x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.trans_halfRight
decls.statement:
theorem trans_halfRight (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (G : Isotopy f₁ f₂) (s : I) (x : X) :
    (F.toHomotopy.trans G.toHomotopy) (halfRight s, x) = G.toHomotopy (s, x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.trans
decls.doc:
Concatenate two isotopies: the result follows `F` on `[0, 1 / 2]` and `G` on `[1 / 2, 1]`,
with the time parameter rescaled linearly. The concatenated total map is an embedding because it
is one on each closed half (where it is `F`'s or `G`'s total embedding, reparametrised), and these
glue along the closed cover `{(t, y) | t ≤ 1 / 2}`, `{(t, y) | 1 / 2 ≤ t}` of the codomain.
decls.statement:
def trans {f₂ : C(X, Y)} (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (G : Isotopy f₁ f₂) :
    Isotopy f₀ f₂

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.trans_apply
decls.doc:
The value of a concatenated isotopy is given by the first isotopy on `[0, 1 / 2]`
and by the second isotopy on `[1 / 2, 1]`, with the time parameter rescaled linearly.
decls.statement:
theorem trans_apply {f₂ : C(X, Y)}
    (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (G : Isotopy f₁ f₂) (x : I × X) :
    (F.trans G) x =
      if h : (x.1 : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2 then
        F (⟨2 * x.1, (unitInterval.mul_pos_mem_iff zero_lt_two).2 ⟨x.1.2.1, h⟩⟩, x.2)
      else
        G (⟨2 * x.1 - 1,
          unitInterval.two_mul_sub_one_mem_iff.2 ⟨(not_le.1 h).le, x.1.2.2⟩⟩, x.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.instHomotopyLike
decls.statement: instance instHomotopyLike : HomotopyLike (Isotopy f₀ f₁) f₀ f₁

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic
decls.doc:
Two maps `f₀ f₁ : C(X, Y)` are **isotopic** if there is an isotopy between them.

Warning: for classical knot theory this non-ambient relation is too coarse: it need not preserve
knot complements, so knot invariants must be built on `AmbientIsotopic`, not on `Isotopic`.
decls.statement: def Isotopic (f₀ f₁ : C(X, Y)) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.of_isotopy
decls.doc: An isotopy witnesses that its endpoints are isotopic.
decls.statement: theorem of_isotopy (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) : Isotopic f₀ f₁

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.refl
decls.doc: Isotopy is reflexive on embeddings.
decls.statement: theorem refl (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : IsEmbedding f) : Isotopic f f

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.symm
decls.doc: Isotopy is symmetric.
decls.statement: theorem symm (h : Isotopic f₀ f₁) : Isotopic f₁ f₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.trans
decls.doc: Isotopy is transitive.
decls.statement:
theorem trans {f₂ : C(X, Y)}
    (h₀₁ : Isotopic f₀ f₁) (h₁₂ : Isotopic f₁ f₂) : Isotopic f₀ f₂

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.isEmbedding_left
decls.doc: The left endpoint of an isotopy relation is an embedding.
decls.statement: theorem isEmbedding_left (h : Isotopic f₀ f₁) : IsEmbedding f₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.isEmbedding_right
decls.doc: The right endpoint of an isotopy relation is an embedding.
decls.statement: theorem isEmbedding_right (h : Isotopic f₀ f₁) : IsEmbedding f₁

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.homotopic
decls.doc: Isotopic maps are homotopic.
decls.statement: theorem homotopic (h : Isotopic f₀ f₁) : Homotopic f₀ f₁

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.homotopicWith
decls.doc: Isotopic maps are homotopic through embeddings in Mathlib's generic API.
decls.statement:
theorem homotopicWith (h : Isotopic f₀ f₁) :
    HomotopicWith f₀ f₁ fun g : C(X, Y) => IsEmbedding g

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy
decls.doc:
An **ambient isotopy** of `Y` is a homotopy from the identity map of `Y` whose
level-preserving total map is a homeomorphism. The time-`1` map `Φ.final` is the resulting
homeomorphism.
decls.statement: structure AmbientIsotopy (Y : Type*) [TopologicalSpace Y] extends C(I × Y, Y)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.totalMap
decls.doc: The level-preserving total map of an ambient isotopy.
decls.statement: def totalMap : C(I × Y, I × Y)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.totalMap_apply
decls.statement: theorem totalMap_apply (p : I × Y) : Φ.totalMap p = (p.1, Φ.toContinuousMap p)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.isHomeomorph_total
decls.doc: The level-preserving total map of an ambient isotopy is a homeomorphism.
decls.statement: theorem isHomeomorph_total : IsHomeomorph Φ.totalMap

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.isHomeomorph_apply
decls.doc: Every time-slice of an ambient isotopy is a self-homeomorphism of `Y`.
decls.statement: theorem isHomeomorph_apply (t : I) : IsHomeomorph fun y => Φ.toContinuousMap (t, y)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.map_zero_left
decls.doc: The ambient isotopy starts at the identity of `Y`.
decls.statement: theorem map_zero_left (y : Y) : Φ.toContinuousMap (0, y) = y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.final
decls.doc: The time-`1` homeomorphism produced by an ambient isotopy, as a continuous map.
decls.statement: def final : C(Y, Y)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.final_apply
decls.statement: theorem final_apply (y : Y) : Φ.final y = Φ.toContinuousMap (1, y)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.isHomeomorph_final
decls.doc: The final map produced by an ambient isotopy is a homeomorphism.
decls.statement: theorem isHomeomorph_final : IsHomeomorph Φ.final

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.homeomorph
decls.doc: The time-`t` self-homeomorphism bundled as a `Homeomorph`.
decls.statement: def homeomorph (t : I) : Y ≃ₜ Y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.homeomorph_apply
decls.statement: theorem homeomorph_apply (t : I) (y : Y) : Φ.homeomorph t y = Φ.toContinuousMap (t, y)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.finalHomeomorph
decls.doc: The time-`1` homeomorphism produced by an ambient isotopy.
decls.statement: def finalHomeomorph : Y ≃ₜ Y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.finalHomeomorph_apply
decls.statement: theorem finalHomeomorph_apply (y : Y) : Φ.finalHomeomorph y = Φ.final y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.refl
decls.doc: The constant ambient isotopy at the identity.
decls.statement: def refl (Y : Type*) [TopologicalSpace Y] : AmbientIsotopy Y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.final_refl
decls.doc: The final map of the constant ambient isotopy is the identity.
decls.statement: theorem final_refl (y : Y) : (refl Y).final y = y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.homeomorph_refl
decls.doc: Every time slice of the constant ambient isotopy is the identity homeomorphism.
decls.statement: theorem homeomorph_refl (t : I) : (refl Y).homeomorph t = Homeomorph.refl Y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.finalHomeomorph_refl
decls.doc: The final homeomorphism of the constant ambient isotopy is the identity.
decls.statement: theorem finalHomeomorph_refl : (refl Y).finalHomeomorph = Homeomorph.refl Y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.instInhabited
decls.statement: instance : Inhabited (AmbientIsotopy Y)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.isotopy_totalMap_eq
decls.statement:
theorem isotopy_totalMap_eq {f : C(X, Y)} :
    (fun p : I × X => (p.1, Φ.toContinuousMap (p.1, f p.2))) =
      Φ.totalMap ∘ Prod.map id f

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.isotopy
decls.doc:
An ambient isotopy carries any embedding `f` to the embedding `Φ.final ∘ f` through an
explicit isotopy: at time `t` the embedding is the homeomorphism `Φ t` postcomposed with `f`.
decls.statement: def isotopy {f : C(X, Y)} (hf : IsEmbedding f) : Isotopy f (Φ.final.comp f)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.isotopy_apply
decls.statement:
theorem isotopy_apply {f : C(X, Y)} (hf : IsEmbedding f) (t : I) (x : X) :
    Φ.isotopy hf (t, x) = Φ.toContinuousMap (t, f x)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.isotopic
decls.doc:
**Ambient isotopy implies isotopy**: an ambient isotopy of `Y` carries any embedding `f`
into `Y` to the isotopic embedding `Φ.final ∘ f`.
decls.title: Ambient isotopy implies isotopy
decls.statement: theorem isotopic {f : C(X, Y)} (hf : IsEmbedding f) : Isotopic f (Φ.final.comp f)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.totalHomeomorph
decls.doc:
The level-preserving total map of an ambient isotopy, bundled as a self-homeomorphism of
`I × Y`.
decls.statement: def totalHomeomorph : (I × Y) ≃ₜ (I × Y)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.totalHomeomorph_apply
decls.statement:
theorem totalHomeomorph_apply (p : I × Y) :
    Φ.totalHomeomorph p = (p.1, Φ.toContinuousMap p)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.totalHomeomorph_symm_fst
decls.doc: The inverse total homeomorphism preserves the time coordinate.
decls.statement: theorem totalHomeomorph_symm_fst (p : I × Y) : (Φ.totalHomeomorph.symm p).1 = p.1

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.trans
decls.doc: **Composition of ambient isotopies**: follow `Φ_t` then `Ψ_t` at each time `t`.
decls.title: Composition of ambient isotopies
decls.statement: def trans (Ψ : AmbientIsotopy Y) : AmbientIsotopy Y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.trans_apply
decls.statement:
theorem trans_apply (Ψ : AmbientIsotopy Y) (p : I × Y) :
    (Φ.trans Ψ).toContinuousMap p = Ψ.toContinuousMap (p.1, Φ.toContinuousMap p)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.final_trans
decls.doc:
The final map of the composite ambient isotopy `Φ.trans Ψ` is the composition of the final
maps of `Φ` and `Ψ`: at the endpoint it is `Ψ.final ∘ Φ.final`.
decls.statement:
theorem final_trans (Ψ : AmbientIsotopy Y) (y : Y) :
    (Φ.trans Ψ).final y = Ψ.final (Φ.final y)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.homeomorph_trans
decls.doc:
Every time slice of a composite ambient isotopy is the composite of the corresponding
time slices.
decls.statement:
theorem homeomorph_trans (Ψ : AmbientIsotopy Y) (t : I) :
    (Φ.trans Ψ).homeomorph t = (Φ.homeomorph t).trans (Ψ.homeomorph t)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.finalHomeomorph_trans
decls.doc:
The final homeomorphism of a composite ambient isotopy is the composite of the final
homeomorphisms.
decls.statement:
theorem finalHomeomorph_trans (Ψ : AmbientIsotopy Y) :
    (Φ.trans Ψ).finalHomeomorph = Φ.finalHomeomorph.trans Ψ.finalHomeomorph

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.symm
decls.doc: **Inverse of an ambient isotopy**: undo `Φ_t` at each time `t`.
decls.title: Inverse of an ambient isotopy
decls.statement: def symm : AmbientIsotopy Y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem symm_apply (p : I × Y) :
    Φ.symm.toContinuousMap p = (Φ.totalHomeomorph.symm p).2

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.symm_final_final
decls.doc:
The inverse ambient isotopy undoes the original: its final map is a left inverse of the
original final map.
decls.statement: theorem symm_final_final (y : Y) : Φ.symm.final (Φ.final y) = y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.final_symm_final
decls.doc:
The original ambient isotopy undoes its inverse: the original final map is a left inverse of
the inverse final map.
decls.statement: theorem final_symm_final (y : Y) : Φ.final (Φ.symm.final y) = y

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.homeomorph_symm
decls.doc:
Every time slice of the inverse ambient isotopy is the inverse of the corresponding
time slice.
decls.statement: theorem homeomorph_symm (t : I) : Φ.symm.homeomorph t = (Φ.homeomorph t).symm

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.finalHomeomorph_symm
decls.doc: The final homeomorphism of the inverse ambient isotopy is the inverse final homeomorphism.
decls.statement: theorem finalHomeomorph_symm : Φ.symm.finalHomeomorph = Φ.finalHomeomorph.symm

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.postcomp
decls.doc:
Postcompose an isotopy `f₀ ≈ f₁` with a topological embedding `g : Y ↪ Z` to get an
isotopy `g ∘ f₀ ≈ g ∘ f₁`.
decls.statement:
def postcomp (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (g : C(Y, Z)) (hg : IsEmbedding g) :
    Isotopy (g.comp f₀) (g.comp f₁)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.postcomp_apply
decls.statement:
theorem postcomp_apply (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (g : C(Y, Z)) (hg : IsEmbedding g) (p : I × X) :
    F.postcomp g hg p = g (F p)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.precomp
decls.doc:
Precompose an isotopy `f₀ ≈ f₁` with a topological embedding `e : W ↪ X` to get an
isotopy `f₀ ∘ e ≈ f₁ ∘ e`.
decls.statement:
def precomp (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (e : C(W, X)) (he : IsEmbedding e) :
    Isotopy (f₀.comp e) (f₁.comp e)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.precomp_apply
decls.statement:
theorem precomp_apply (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (e : C(W, X)) (he : IsEmbedding e) (p : I × W) :
    F.precomp e he p = F (p.1, e p.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.postcomp
decls.doc:
Postcompose an isotopy relation with a topological embedding: if `f₀ ≈ f₁` and `g` is an
embedding, then `g ∘ f₀ ≈ g ∘ f₁`.
decls.statement:
theorem postcomp (h : Isotopic f₀ f₁) (g : C(Y, Z)) (hg : IsEmbedding g) :
    Isotopic (g.comp f₀) (g.comp f₁)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.precomp
decls.doc:
Precompose an isotopy relation with a topological embedding: if `f₀ ≈ f₁` and `e` is an
embedding, then `f₀ ∘ e ≈ f₁ ∘ e`.
decls.statement:
theorem precomp (h : Isotopic f₀ f₁) (e : C(W, X)) (he : IsEmbedding e) :
    Isotopic (f₀.comp e) (f₁.comp e)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.postcomp_precomp
decls.doc:
The two-sided form: an isotopy relation survives composing with an embedding on each
side.
decls.statement:
theorem postcomp_precomp (h : Isotopic f₀ f₁) (g : C(Y, Z)) (hg : IsEmbedding g) (e : C(W, X))
    (he : IsEmbedding e) : Isotopic (g.comp (f₀.comp e)) (g.comp (f₁.comp e))

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.postcomp_homeomorph
decls.doc: Postcomposing an isotopy relation with a homeomorphism of the codomain.
decls.statement:
theorem postcomp_homeomorph (h : Isotopic f₀ f₁) (e : Y ≃ₜ Z) :
    Isotopic ((e : C(Y, Z)).comp f₀) ((e : C(Y, Z)).comp f₁)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.precomp_homeomorph
decls.doc: Precomposing an isotopy relation with a homeomorphism of the source.
decls.statement:
theorem precomp_homeomorph (h : Isotopic f₀ f₁) (e : W ≃ₜ X) :
    Isotopic (f₀.comp (e : C(W, X))) (f₁.comp (e : C(W, X)))

decls.name: TauCeti.isEmbedding_dupTime
decls.doc:
The time-duplicating map `(t, (x, x')) ↦ ((t, x), (t, x'))` is a topological embedding: it has
the continuous left inverse `((a, x), (b, x')) ↦ (a, (x, x'))`.
decls.statement:
theorem isEmbedding_dupTime :
    IsEmbedding fun p : I × (X × X') => ((p.1, p.2.1), (p.1, p.2.2))

decls.name: TauCeti.isEmbedding_mergeTotal
decls.doc:
The core embedding lemma shared by the isotopy and ambient-isotopy products. If `u` and `v` are
embeddings of `I × X → I × Y` and `I × X' → I × Y'` that preserve the time coordinate, then the
*merged* total map `(t, (x, x')) ↦ (t, ((u (t, x)).2, (v (t, x')).2))` reading both at the same
time `t` is an embedding. It factors as the time-duplicating embedding, then `u × v`, then the
projection identifying the two (equal) time coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem isEmbedding_mergeTotal {u : C(I × X, I × Y)} {v : C(I × X', I × Y')}
    (hu : IsEmbedding u) (hv : IsEmbedding v) (hu1 : ∀ p, (u p).1 = p.1)
    (hv1 : ∀ p, (v p).1 = p.1) :
    IsEmbedding fun p : I × (X × X') => (p.1, ((u (p.1, p.2.1)).2, (v (p.1, p.2.2)).2))

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.prodMap
decls.doc:
The **product of two isotopies**, sharing the time parameter: from an isotopy `f₀ ≈ f₁` and an
isotopy `g₀ ≈ g₁` build an isotopy `f₀.prodMap g₀ ≈ f₁.prodMap g₁` whose value at `(t, (x, x'))` is
`(F (t, x), G (t, x'))`. The underlying homotopy is Mathlib's `ContinuousMap.Homotopy.prodMap`; the
total map is an embedding by `isEmbedding_mergeTotal`.
decls.statement:
def prodMap (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (G : Isotopy g₀ g₁) :
    Isotopy (f₀.prodMap g₀) (f₁.prodMap g₁)

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopy.prodMap_apply
decls.statement:
theorem prodMap_apply (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (G : Isotopy g₀ g₁) (p : I × (X × X')) :
    F.prodMap G p = (F (p.1, p.2.1), G (p.1, p.2.2))

decls.name: TauCeti.Isotopic.prodMap
decls.doc:
Products preserve the isotopy relation: if `f₀ ≈ f₁` and `g₀ ≈ g₁`, then
`f₀.prodMap g₀ ≈ f₁.prodMap g₁`.
decls.statement:
theorem prodMap (h : Isotopic f₀ f₁) (h' : Isotopic g₀ g₁) :
    Isotopic (f₀.prodMap g₀) (f₁.prodMap g₁)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.prodCongr
decls.doc:
The **product of two ambient isotopies**, sharing the time parameter: from an ambient isotopy
`Φ` of `Y` and one `Ψ` of `Y'` build an ambient isotopy of `Y × Y'` whose value at `(t, (y, y'))`
is `(Φ (t, y), Ψ (t, y'))`. Its total map is a homeomorphism, being an embedding (by
`isEmbedding_mergeTotal`) and surjective (each factor is surjective at every time, by
`AmbientIsotopy.isHomeomorph_apply`).
decls.statement: def prodCongr (Φ : AmbientIsotopy Y) (Ψ : AmbientIsotopy Y') : AmbientIsotopy (Y × Y')

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.prodCongr_apply
decls.statement:
theorem prodCongr_apply (Φ : AmbientIsotopy Y) (Ψ : AmbientIsotopy Y') (p : I × (Y × Y')) :
    (Φ.prodCongr Ψ).toContinuousMap p =
      (Φ.toContinuousMap (p.1, p.2.1), Ψ.toContinuousMap (p.1, p.2.2))

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy.final_prodCongr
decls.doc: The final map of a product ambient isotopy is the product of the two final maps.
decls.statement:
theorem final_prodCongr (Φ : AmbientIsotopy Y) (Ψ : AmbientIsotopy Y') (y : Y × Y') :
    (Φ.prodCongr Ψ).final y = (Φ.final y.1, Ψ.final y.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.AmbientIsotopic.prodMap
decls.doc:
Products preserve the ambient-isotopy relation: if `f` and `f'` are ambient isotopic in `Y` and
`g` and `g'` are ambient isotopic in `Y'`, then `f.prodMap g` and `f'.prodMap g'` are ambient
isotopic in `Y × Y'`, via the product ambient isotopy.
decls.statement:
theorem prodMap (h : AmbientIsotopic f f') (h' : AmbientIsotopic g g') :
    AmbientIsotopic (f.prodMap g) (f'.prodMap g')

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.monodromy_eq_self_iff_mem_range
decls.doc:
A loop class of the base fixes a chosen lift `e` of the basepoint under monodromy exactly
when it is the image of a loop class of the total space based at `e`.

The image subgroup on the right is the subgroup of `π₁(X, x)` that the classification of covers
attaches to the pointed cover `(E, e)`.
decls.statement:
theorem monodromy_eq_self_iff_mem_range (hp : IsCoveringMap p) (e : p ⁻¹' {x})
    (γ : FundamentalGroup X x) :
    hp.monodromy γ e = e ↔
      γ ∈ (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ e.2).range

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.stabilizer_eq_range
decls.doc:
The stabiliser of a chosen lift `e` of the basepoint, for the monodromy action of
`π₁(X, x)` on the fibre over `x`, is the image of `π₁(E, e)` under the covering map.
decls.statement:
theorem stabilizer_eq_range (hp : IsCoveringMap p) (e : p ⁻¹' {x}) :
    letI

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.exists_monodromy_eq_of_joined
decls.doc:
A path joining two lifts of the basepoint projects to a loop of the base whose monodromy
carries the first lift to the second.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_monodromy_eq_of_joined (hp : IsCoveringMap p) {e e' : p ⁻¹' {x}}
    (h : Joined (e : E) (e' : E)) : ∃ γ : FundamentalGroup X x, hp.monodromy γ e = e'

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.exists_monodromy_eq
decls.doc: On a fibre of a path-connected cover, monodromy is transitive.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_monodromy_eq [PathConnectedSpace E] (hp : IsCoveringMap p) (e e' : p ⁻¹' {x}) :
    ∃ γ : FundamentalGroup X x, hp.monodromy γ e = e'

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.monodromy_isPretransitive
decls.doc: The monodromy action of `π₁(X, x)` on a fibre of a path-connected cover is transitive.
decls.statement:
theorem monodromy_isPretransitive [PathConnectedSpace E] (hp : IsCoveringMap p) (x : X) :
    letI

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.fiberEquivQuotientRange
decls.doc:
**Orbit-stabiliser for a covering map.** Choosing a lift `e` of the basepoint identifies the
fibre over `x` with the coset space of the subgroup of `π₁(X, x)` recovered from `(E, e)`,
provided the cover is path connected.
decls.title: Orbit-stabiliser for a covering map
decls.statement:
def fiberEquivQuotientRange [PathConnectedSpace E] (hp : IsCoveringMap p)
    (e : p ⁻¹' {x}) :
    p ⁻¹' {x} ≃
      FundamentalGroup X x ⧸ (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ e.2).range

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.fiberEquivQuotientRange_symm_apply_mk
decls.doc:
The inverse of the orbit-stabiliser identification sends the coset of a loop class to the
monodromy translate of the chosen lift.
decls.statement:
theorem fiberEquivQuotientRange_symm_apply_mk [PathConnectedSpace E] (hp : IsCoveringMap p)
    (e : p ⁻¹' {x}) (γ : FundamentalGroup X x) :
    (fiberEquivQuotientRange hp e).symm (QuotientGroup.mk γ) = hp.monodromy γ e

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.card_fiber_eq_index
decls.doc: **The number of sheets of a path-connected cover is the index of the recovered subgroup.**
decls.title: The number of sheets of a path-connected cover is the index of the recovered subgroup
decls.statement:
theorem card_fiber_eq_index [PathConnectedSpace E] (hp : IsCoveringMap p) (e : p ⁻¹' {x}) :
    Nat.card (p ⁻¹' {x}) =
      (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ e.2).range.index

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.range_mapOfEq_monodromy
decls.doc: Moving the chosen lift by monodromy conjugates the recovered subgroup.
decls.statement:
theorem range_mapOfEq_monodromy (hp : IsCoveringMap p) (e : p ⁻¹' {x})
    (γ : FundamentalGroup X x) :
    (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ (hp.monodromy γ e).2).range =
      ((FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ e.2).range).map
        (MulAut.conj γ).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.exists_range_eq_map_conj_of_joined
decls.doc: Two lifts of the basepoint joined by a path in the cover recover conjugate subgroups.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_range_eq_map_conj_of_joined (hp : IsCoveringMap p) {e e' : p ⁻¹' {x}}
    (h : Joined (e : E) (e' : E)) :
    ∃ γ : FundamentalGroup X x,
      (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ e'.2).range =
        ((FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ e.2).range).map
          (MulAut.conj γ).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.exists_range_eq_map_conj
decls.doc:
On a path-connected cover, any two lifts of the basepoint recover conjugate subgroups: an
unpointed connected cover determines only the conjugacy class of the subgroup.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_range_eq_map_conj [PathConnectedSpace E] (hp : IsCoveringMap p)
    (e e' : p ⁻¹' {x}) :
    ∃ γ : FundamentalGroup X x,
      (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ e'.2).range =
        ((FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ e.2).range).map
          (MulAut.conj γ).toMonoidHom

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.normal_range_iff
decls.doc:
On a path-connected cover, the subgroup recovered from a lift of the basepoint is normal
exactly when it does not depend on which lift is chosen. This is the subgroup-side criterion for
the cover to be regular.
decls.statement:
theorem normal_range_iff [PathConnectedSpace E] (hp : IsCoveringMap p) (e : p ⁻¹' {x}) :
    (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ e.2).range.Normal ↔
      ∀ e' : p ⁻¹' {x},
        (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ e'.2).range =
          (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ e.2).range

decls.name: Path.codRestrict
decls.doc:
Restrict a path whose image lies in a subset to a path in the corresponding subtype.
The source and target are the given subtype endpoints, and coercing the restricted path back to
`X` recovers the original path pointwise.

decls.name: Path.codRestrict_coe
decls.doc: The underlying point of `γ.codRestrict hmem` at time `t` is just `γ t`, viewed in `X`.
decls.statement:
theorem codRestrict_coe {s : Set X} {x y : s} (γ : Path x.val y.val)
    (hmem : ∀ t, γ t ∈ s) (t : I) :
    (γ.codRestrict hmem t : X) = γ t

decls.name: Path.map_codRestrict
decls.doc: Mapping `γ.codRestrict hmem` back along the subtype inclusion recovers `γ`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_codRestrict {s : Set X} {x y : s} (γ : Path x.val y.val)
    (hmem : ∀ t, γ t ∈ s) :
    (γ.codRestrict hmem).map continuous_subtype_val = γ

decls.name: Path.truncateOfLE_range_subset
decls.doc:
If the extended path stays inside `U` throughout `[t₀, t₁]`, then the truncated subpath has
range in `U`.

decls.name: Path.initialSegmentFamily
decls.doc:
The family of initial segments of `γ : Path a b`: at parameter `t : I`, the path
